vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: agentcanary
Version: 1.0.2

The skill bundle is a documentation-only package providing instructions for an AI agent to interact with the AgentCanary financial intelligence API. It contains no executable code, scripts, or local filesystem access, and its instructions are strictly limited to fetching market data and sentiment analysis from the 'api.agentcanary.ai' domain. The service uses a transparent tiered pricing model based on crypto deposits for API credits.

llm.summary: The skill's declared purpose (market intelligence API) matches its instructions and requirements — it is an instruction-only wrapper around an external HTTP API and does not request unrelated system access or secrets — but users should be cautious about on-chain payments and API-key handling.

dimensions.detail: Name/description describe a market-intelligence HTTP API. The skill is instruction-only and requires no local binaries, environment variables, or special install — this aligns with an API-only integration that uses API keys issued by the service.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs agents to create API keys (POST /keys/create) and to include the apiKey as a query param for requests. It explicitly disallows local execution and filesystem access. One operational risk: passing apiKey as a query parameter can expose keys in logs or traces if the agent or platform logs outgoing URLs; the skill text claims 'no secrets in prompt' but does not provide secure handling guidance for keys (e.g., store in secure agent vault vs inline in messages). Otherwise, endpoints and polling patterns are scoped to market intelligence and do not instruct reading unrelated files or system state.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec and no code files; the skill is instruction-only, which is the lowest-risk install mechanism and consistent with the claimed API-only behavior.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requires no environment variables or platform credentials, which is proportionate. However, authentication is wallet-based via on-chain deposits and an apiKey issued by the service; this requires the user to send funds to the service's deposit address. The SKILL.md claims 'same deposit address on all chains' (unusual but plausible), and 'no KYC' / low minimum deposits increase financial risk (funds sent to an unknown/opaque provider cannot be recovered easily).
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill does not request persistent system privileges, does not modify other skills, and has no install-time setup — no elevated persistence or privilege is requested.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to be a straightforward wrapper for an external market-intelligence API and is internally consistent. Main practical risks are non-technical: you must deposit on-chain funds to the provider and then use an issued apiKey. Before using: (1) verify the vendor website and reputation (the registry source is unknown); (2) test with the smallest possible deposit or a throwaway wallet to limit financial loss; (3) avoid pasting the apiKey into LLM prompts or public logs—store and use it via a secure vault/mechanism if your agent platform supports it, because query-parameter keys can be captured in logs; (4) review billing/withdrawal/KYC terms on the provider site; and (5) monitor any agent network logs to ensure keys or wallet details are not being leaked. If you need higher assurance, ask the publisher for a verifiable homepage/source code or for the API's security whitepaper before depositing funds.
